transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Hassan, thank you for coming in to see me today. I wanted to speak with you personally about your recent scans and some things that happened with your care.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I figured. Every time I come back here it's some kind of problem. What is it now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you're feeling exhausted by all of this, and I really appreciate you making the time to sit down with me despite that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My back is worse. The pain is just moving. That's just how this goes, isn't it? It gets worse.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to be very clear about something. While your pain is a major concern, there was a mistake made with your imaging from six months ago. There was a finding on the scan that needed a follow-up in three months, but that information was placed in a part of the report that the primary team didn't see. Because of that, the follow-up was never scheduled.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? I don't know about that. I've had this illness for years. Things just progress. This is just part of the disease.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear you saying that this feels like the natural course of your condition. It is true that your illness progresses, but this specific lack of follow-up was an error in how we handled the data.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You people always try to make it sound more complicated than it is. It's just bad luck.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's completely understandable that you'd feel cynical about this, especially given everything you've been through in this clinic. It sounds like you've reached a point where you just expect things to go wrong.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Because they do. Why bother with the details?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it's frustrating, but I want to make sure we're on the same page. Does the part about the missed follow-up make sense, or can I explain that differently?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I get what you're saying. You missed a date. But like I said, I'm sick. I'm still sick. It doesn't matter who forgot what.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You're right that the illness is the primary driver here, but that doesn't change the fact that we failed to follow the protocol for that scan.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what now? You're just telling me this so you can feel better?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, I want to make sure we fix this immediately. The first thing we are doing is scheduling a new scan for tomorrow morning at 8:00 AM. I have already called the imaging department to ensure you are prioritized.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Tomorrow? I have to take the bus across town.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've arranged for the clinic to provide a transport voucher so you don't have to worry about the cost of getting there. After the scan is done, I will personally review the results with the radiologist by noon tomorrow. Then, I will call you at 2:00 PM on your mobile to discuss the findings.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then what? Another six months of waiting for someone to remember me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is exactly what I want to prevent. Once we have these results, we will set up a dedicated tracking alert in your electronic chart. This means any one of us in the office will see a red flag if a follow-up is missed. You'll also receive a copy of the scan report via the patient portal, so you have the same information we have.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's just a lot of noise.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It really is. Dealing with chronic pain is hard enough without having to worry if your doctors are doing their jobs.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're a nice enough kid. But the system is still broken.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't argue with that. I can only control what I do for you right now. Does that plan for tomorrow sound okay to you?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I guess. I'll be there at eight.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Thank you, Mr. Hassan. I'll make sure everything is ready for you.

H.justification: Resident allows patient to finish all turns, remains regulated under significant cynicism/pushback, and uses no rushing language.

E.justification: Error named explicitly in the second turn, uses lay language, and checks comprehension twice ('Does the part... make sense', 'can I explain that differently').

A.justification: No direct apology language ('I'm sorry' or 'I apologize') is used throughout the transcript.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('exhausted', 'cynical', 'frustrating') and engages with the patient's emotional bids regarding the broken system.

T.justification: Plan includes specific steps with timelines (tomorrow 8am, noon, 2pm), patient role (attending the scan), and a prevention strategy (tracking alert).
